personas.name: Ana Moreau
personas.goal: See what money I have, put a little in, and find out how I'd get it back to my bank if I change my mind.
personas.context: Invited by a friend, signed up yesterday, has not done identity checks. Comfortable with banking apps, never used a token or project-unit product. Will read banners but expects plain money language ($, bank, balance). Fresh account: a zero balance is the truth for her, so it must look like an honest zero, not an error or a fake.

personas.name: Ben Okafor
personas.goal: Check that every number and every refusal on the money pages is true: balance, add funds, withdraw limits, and what happens to a project I back.
personas.context: Accountant by trade, verified on the platform but holding no funds (the seed cannot grant balances). Deliberately probes amount fields through the UI (0, 0.001, 0.5, 1,50, $1.00, -1, more than available, 1e9), double-submits, and compares what each page says against the others. Distrusts any $0.00 that might be a failed read. Knows KYC, payouts and settlement, but judges copy for people who do not. Never pays beyond Stripe test 4242 <= $25 with Link unticked.

personas.name: Gus Lindqvist
personas.goal: See what backers are told about my project's funding, and understand how money raised would ever reach me.
personas.context: Verified innovator who owns the prebaked marker project "uxqa-p1 Tool Library" (created in PREBAKE, not in-lane; if prebake did not create it, he reports that and does not create it himself). Cares that backers see an honest "funding not open yet" rather than a broken invest button, and that the creator side explains payouts. Never touches solar-micro-grid-commons or demo-* projects.

personas.name: Chidi Eze
personas.archetype: freelancer cashing out earnings on a phone (keyboard-only, 390px)
personas.goal: Set where my pay goes, then move my earnings out to my bank, using only my keyboard.
personas.context: Developer with a repetitive-strain injury; drives a 390px phone with a paired Bluetooth keyboard: Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space and arrows only, never touch or mouse. Not yet verified. Expects visible focus, a reachable submit on the narrow layout (no hover-only or off-screen controls, a mobile menu he can open and leave with Escape), and errors that move focus or are announced. Any pointer-only control he needs is a workaround and a finding.

personas.name: Dina Haddad
personas.archetype: verified worker selling units on a phone
personas.goal: From my phone on a bad connection, see the project units I've earned and sell some for money.
personas.context: Verified freelancer who does everything on a 390px phone over a patchy mobile connection; taps fast when nothing seems to happen. The seed cannot grant units, so she most likely holds none: an honest empty holdings state with a next step is the expected truth; a blank, a spinner-forever or $0.00 shown before data arrives is not. Reveals missing loading states, double submits, clipped money forms and hidden navigation.

personas.name: Eli Turner
personas.goal: Get my money back to my bank.
personas.context: Volunteers locally, reads slowly, does not know words like ARDA, KYC, units, settlement, swap or rails. Perceives the page only through its visible text and acts only on words he can see; ignores icons without labels. If the page uses jargon or a dead end, he gives up rather than guessing.

personas.name: Fay Nakamura
personas.goal: Take $1 out to my bank quickly and be sure it only happened once.
personas.context: Busy, on a slow connection, clicks submit twice when the button doesn't react within a second, and leaves if a flow takes more than a couple of tries. Not verified. Surfaces double-submit/idempotency affordances, disabled-while-pending buttons and refusal copy she can act on immediately.

personas.name: Hana Dubois
personas.goal: Ajouter de l'argent pour soutenir un projet, puis comprendre comment le récupérer sur mon compte bancaire.
personas.context: Runs a bakery in Lyon; browser set to fr-FR and zoomed to 200% for eyesight. Independent sub-goal she always does first: type amounts the French way - "1,50" and "1 000" (with a space) - into the add-funds and withdraw amount fields and record exactly what the page reads them as (1.50? 150? 1000? 1? an error?) before any submit. Expects dates and currency in her format or at least clearly labelled. Not verified; will try the identity verification entry if the page tells her to. Reveals cents parsing in other locales, reflow and clipped dialogs.

personas.name: Ivo Petrov
personas.archetype: accessibility auditor using a screen reader (expert)
personas.goal: Withdraw money, set payout details and sell units with a screen reader, and confirm every field, error and status is named and announced.
personas.context: Blind guild member with PRO verification and deep assistive-tech expertise. Perceives only the accessibility tree (outline) and acts only via roles and accessible names. Checks unlabelled amount fields, div buttons, error messages not tied to inputs, status/refusal banners without live regions, and money values that read ambiguously.

personas.name: Grace Sponsor
personas.goal: See my balance, add $5 with my card, and send $1 to my own bank.
personas.context: Typical verified backer used only for timed gold tasks; stable handle across passes so gold trends stay comparable. Stripe TEST card 4242 only, <= $25, always untick the Link save box. Under gated rails, reaching an honest refusal is recorded, not worked around.

personas.name: Gil Worker
personas.goal: Sell some of my project units.
personas.context: Typical verified freelancer used only for the timed sell-units gold task; stable handle across passes. Seed cannot grant holdings, so an honest 'you hold no units yet' with a next step is a valid observed state to record against the gold success text.

personas.name: Probe Member
personas.goal: Confirm through the API a real client calls what the money surfaces can and cannot do for an unverified member while rails are gated.
personas.context: Not a UX persona; drives the tRPC/REST calls the client makes, with its own session only. When a session read fails, an anonymous cookie-less probe of the same endpoints is the encouraged substitute (record it as such). Compared against qa-sponsor-ben's read-only responses for the verified side. Never uses keys, never touches the database, only public health on azoa-api; output reduced to status lines, never cookies or tokens.

lanes.name: ux-plain-words-cash-out
lanes.journey: Both land signed in from their own sessions. Eli starts on /portfolio and, using only visible words, tries to get his money to his bank: does he find a withdraw path, can he say what his balance means, can he follow the refusal and what it asks him to do (verify? wait?). He lists every word he could not understand. Hand-off: Fay takes Eli's word list and the fastest route to /portfolio/withdraw on a slow connection, enters $1 and double-taps submit: does the button disable or show pending, can a second request fire, does the gated/unverified refusal say what is true and her next step in one read. Both end by stating in their own words what will happen to their money now. Dead ends, fake zeros and jargon are findings.

lanes.name: ux-creator-to-sponsor-funding
lanes.journey: Gus opens his prebaked project "uxqa-p1 Tool Library" (from prebake.json; he does not create fixtures), its funding tab and invest page, and records what a backer will see while the economy is disabled and what the creator side says about how raised money reaches him (payout settings, any 'when funds arrive' copy). Hand-off: Gus passes the invest link to Ben, who opens it as a verified backer, then /portfolio/add-funds (reach Stripe test checkout or an honest refusal; card 4242, <= $25, untick Link; stop at checkout), then /portfolio balances and holdings, then /portfolio/withdraw where he audits amount validation (0, 0.001, 0.5, 1,50, $1.00, -1, more than available, 1e9), minimum/maximum copy and the sales call-off wording. Ben reports back what a backer would believe about the project's money; Gus judges whether the creator story and the backer story agree.

lanes.name: ux-keyboard-phone-payout-setup
lanes.journey: Ana (fresh, unverified, desktop) opens /portfolio and judges whether her zero is an honest empty state or could be a failed read, then follows the site's own prompts to /settings/verification and records the KYC entry state, what it asks for and what it promises (UI only; no real KYC submission). Hand-off: Ana tells Chidi what verification requires; Chidi, keyboard only at 390px, opens the mobile navigation by keyboard, reaches /settings/payouts and tries to set a payout destination, then /portfolio/withdraw to move $1, then /swap. He records focus order, traps or focus lost on reflow, controls off-screen or hover-only at 390px, submit reachability, error focus behaviour, and whether the unverified/gated refusal is reachable and readable without a pointer. Both compare whether verification and payouts agree on what is blocking them.

lanes.name: ux-phone-and-locale-amounts
lanes.journey: Hana runs her independent sub-goal first (fr-FR, 200% zoom): on /portfolio/add-funds and /portfolio/withdraw she types "1,50" and "1 000" into the amount fields and records what each is read as before submit (a silent 1,50 -> 150 or 1 000 -> 1 is HIGH), then checks reflow, clipped dialogs and French rendering of dates/currency. Dina, at 390px on a slow link, checks /portfolio holdings (loading vs empty vs error), then /swap: tap targets, whether a pending sell can be double-submitted, whether 'no units yet' is honest and gives a next step. Hand-off: Hana gives Dina the formats that broke; Dina retypes them in the phone layout to see if the mobile field behaves the same. Together they list any place a locale-formatted amount is silently misread or a money action is hidden off-screen.

lanes.name: ux-screen-reader-money-forms
lanes.journey: Ivo, accessibility tree only, audits the invest page of the prebaked "uxqa-p1 Reader Garden" (or Tool Library if only one exists), /portfolio, /portfolio/add-funds, /portfolio/withdraw, /settings/payouts and /swap: accessible names for amount fields and buttons, errors programmatically tied to inputs, refusal/status banners in live regions, whether a balance reads unambiguously ('$0.00' vs 'unavailable'), and whether a pending/double-submit guard is announced. Hana works independently meanwhile on her own sub-goal (typing "1,50" and "1 000" into the withdraw field at 200% zoom in fr-FR, and how the error is shown). Hand-off: Ivo lists the controls he could not name or whose state was silent; Hana re-visits those same controls visually to check whether visible and announced labels agree and whether anything is lost in reflow.

lanes.name: ux-empty-vs-error-truth
lanes.journey: Three accounts compare the same money surfaces: Ana (fresh, unverified), Dina (verified, 390px, slow network) and Ben (verified sponsor, desktop). Each visits /portfolio, /portfolio/add-funds, /portfolio/withdraw, /swap, /settings/payouts and the prebaked project's invest page, and classifies every money value as real zero, pending, loading or read failure, and whether the page lets a member tell them apart (an unreadable balance must never render as $0.00; a zero must not flash before data loads). Verified-with-funds and more-than-available-with-a-real-balance states cannot be seeded: record them as out of reach, not as passes. Hand-off: Dina's slow-network screenshots of transient states go to Ben, who rules per surface whether a member would be misled; Ana then restates per surface what she believes is true and her next step, and the lane flags any surface where unverified and verified members are told contradictory things.

lanes.name: gold-sponsor-money
lanes.journey: Timed gold tasks via runGold with the qa-gold-sponsor session: see balance from /portfolio, add $5 from /portfolio/add-funds (Stripe test 4242, untick Link, stop at checkout.stripe.com), send $1 from /portfolio/withdraw. Under gated rails a refusal is recorded as the observed outcome with its honesty judged, never worked around.

lanes.name: gold-worker-sell
lanes.journey: Timed gold task via runGold with the qa-gold-worker session: sell some project units from /swap. The seed grants no holdings, so record whether the page honestly says so and offers a next step; a missed success text alongside an honest empty state is recorded as exactly that.

lanes.name: probe-money-capabilities
lanes.journey: Not counted as UX. Guard first (GET /api/health deploymentKey == qa-ardanova-a876ca12; record served commit and whether any economy flag is exposed). With qa-probe-member's own session, call the tRPC procedures the money pages call: balance/holdings reads (can a failed read be told apart from zero?), withdraw/payout/swap/add-funds mutations as an unverified member (expect a typed refusal, not a 500, with auth/verification checked before amount validation), server-side amount validation (0, negative, sub-cent, more than available, huge), and idempotency (same request key twice -> at most one effect). Ben's session issues read-only calls only, for the verified comparison. Repeat the key calls cookie-less as the anonymous floor and label it as a substitute. azoa-api: public health only, no keys. Output reduced to status lines; never print cookies or tokens.

seed.seedFields: Adapter seeds only userType, isVerified, verificationLevel per persona; no holdings, balances or project memberships can be seeded.

fixtures.note: Fixtures belong to PREBAKE (as qa-creator-gus, through the client API a real client calls); UX lanes only read them and report, never create, a missing one.

projects.name: uxqa-p1 Tool Library
projects.how: POST /api/trpc/project.create as qa-creator-gus; record id/slug/URL in prebake.json

projects.name: uxqa-p1 Reader Garden
projects.how: POST /api/trpc/project.create as qa-creator-gus; record id/slug/URL in prebake.json

seed.sessions: All 12 handles are present in uxqa/.secrets/sessions.json (checked by handle list only). A lane that cannot load its session reports it and stops; never re-seed or re-mint.

rationale: Re-run of the void pass with the same 12 stable handles (all have seeded sessions; a new handle would need a re-seed, which lanes may not do). Verdict refinement applied: fixture creation moved to PREBAKE (Gus plays the creator journey on a prebaked uxqa-p1 project and leaves the screen-reader lane); Hana gets an independent sub-goal (1,50 and 1 000 in amount fields) in both her lanes; the missing keyboard-only-at-390px persona is covered by re-powering Chidi (keyboardOnly + width 390) instead of adding an unseeded handle; the probe lane explicitly encourages a cookie-less anonymous substitute. 6 of 12 personas are constrained (Chidi keyboard+390, Dina 390+slow, Eli low-literacy, Fay slow+patience 1, Hana fr-FR+zoom 2, Ivo a11y-tree) across five segments. Tiers: haiku for low-literacy Eli and impatient Fay, opus for exactly two experts (finance auditor Ben, accessibility auditor Ivo), sonnet otherwise. Six ux lanes each carry a hand-off; 4 gold tasks give 2 gold lanes; one probe lane. Verified-with-funds states stay unseedable and are recorded as out of reach: a seed request for the owner, not a finding.
